intervention_label: Gating workup run alongside cycle 1: echocardiogram with LVEF and a clinician-documented ECOG (LMS-04 eligibility gates), hepatic and renal panel with CK, germline TP53 consent conversation and draw before genotoxic chemotherapy, retrieval of the September 2024 operative report (morcellation status; gates the lung-directed consolidation branch), a one-pass tumor package off the 2024 block (HRR/BRCA2 NGS with RNA fusion calling, TMB/MSI, MMR IHC, B7-H3 and RB1 IHC, ER/PR specimen provenance) with HLA class I typing, and altitude-read baselines (CBC with reticulocytes and ferritin, PFTs with DLCO, oximetry at 8,500 ft, RECIST baseline CT)
expected_benefit: Clears the two true gates on cycle 1 (baseline LVEF and a documented ECOG were LMS-04 eligibility criteria), returns the germline TP53 result before the cumulative anthracycline plan is fixed, settles whether the 2024 specimen was morcellated (44% vs 12.9% abdominopelvic dissemination, which gates any lung-directed consolidation), and opens or closes nearly every targeted branch in this dossier with one panel, one IHC block and one blood draw, all running in parallel with induction.
key_risks: Time is the only cost, and the tiering matters: LVEF, ECOG and the hepatic-renal panel are gates; DLCO, ferritin, reticulocytes and altitude oximetry are baselines, and veto-grading baselines would delay induction in a patient who already lost 23 months
The germline TP53 draw is a consent conversation with consequences for her relatives, not a scheduling detail; whether she wants germline information at all has never been asked
Tissue allocation on the 2024 block should be agreed in one conversation (pathology review, NGS, IHC set) before any single order exhausts it
An ER/PR result of unverified specimen provenance underlies the endocrine foreclosure; a failed stain on a 2024 block reads identically to a true negative
preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist; every value in preferences.json is an intake default. The workup itself imposes no toxicity and forecloses nothing, and it generates the fitness and biomarker facts any future preference conversation needs.
guideline_status: ESMO Precision Medicine Working Group 2024 recommends tumor NGS in sarcoma; ERN GENTURIS 2020 puts germline TP53 testing before genotoxic chemotherapy; BSG 2025 states morcellation is contraindicated in uterine sarcoma, which upgrades the 2024 operative report to a staging prerequisite; baseline ventricular imaging before anthracycline exposure is standard cardio-oncology practice.
rationale_summary: Every persona ordered some version of this workup, and the disagreement was only about tiering. The conservative pre-registered a veto against induction scheduled over the missing battery, then withdrew it in round 2 because the dossier shows induction imminent and the battery undone, not a cycle 1 date placed over the missing tests; its re-arm clause is explicit, and the day a cycle 1 date lands ahead of the echocardiogram the withdrawal becomes a veto. The risktaker's distinction governs the tiering here: LVEF and cardiac clearance were LMS-04 eligibility criteria and are gates, while DLCO, ferritin, reticulocytes and altitude oximetry are baselines that run alongside cycle 1 rather than ahead of it. The critic's morcellation pick and the concensusite's upgrade of it resolve into this row: BSG 2025's contraindication language plus 44% vs 12.9% abdominopelvic dissemination make the 2024 operative report a staging prerequisite that gates the lung-directed consolidation branch every persona carried, not a therapy and not merely surveillance. The concensusite moved the germline TP53 draw from the parallel track to before cycle 1 per ERN GENTURIS, and the advocate's correction stands: it is a consent conversation with family consequences, and nobody has asked her. One panel, one IHC block and one blood draw open or close nearly every targeted option in this dossier at zero cost in treatment days.
open_questions: Whether she wants germline information at all; the family-consequences conversation has not happened
Whether the ER/PR <1% stain was run on the 2024 primary or the 2026 lung core, and whether internal controls worked
Whether the 2024 block was adequately sampled for a suspected sarcoma (one block per centimetre standard), which the expert pathology review will settle
Whether any imaging exists from the 2024-2026 interval to bound growth kinetics before induction resets the baseline
likelihood_of_effect: Diagnostic gate: LVEF and ECOG clear LMS-04 eligibility; one panel, one IHC block and one blood draw open or close nearly every targeted branch.
toxicity_burden: Low (none — records requests, blood draws, echocardiogram, and stains on archival tissue)

counter_productive_moa.description: Workup row; no mechanism.

overall: Runs alongside induction, not ahead of it: only the echocardiogram, the documented ECOG and two consent conversations are true gates on cycle 1.

intervention_label: Doxorubicin + trabectedin induction, then trabectedin maintenance (LMS-04 regimen), first line
expected_benefit: Median PFS 12.2 vs 6.2 months (adjusted HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.29-0.58; BICR-read pre-specified primary) and median OS 33 vs 24 months (adjusted HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.44-0.95) at 55 months median follow-up, in randomized first-line metastatic leiomyosarcoma (uterine primaries 67/150).
key_risks: G3-4 neutropenia 80%, thrombocytopenia 47%, febrile neutropenia 28% on the combination arm; primary G-CSF prophylaxis belongs in the cycle 1 orders
Cardiotoxicity is a lifetime ledger at 39: cumulative doxorubicin dose planning and a dexrazoxane conversation belong before cycle 1

Maintenance-phase toxicity is thinly published; monitoring defaults to the single-agent trabectedin dossier (G>=3 ALT elevation 25%, rhabdomyolysis 1.2%, treatment-related deaths 2.1%), so CK and LFTs stay on the recurring schedule
Altitude-raised haemoglobin at 8,500 ft will mask chemotherapy anaemia against sea-level reference ranges
A payer denial of the off-label first-line authorization is the one thing that could actually delay induction
preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist; the 0.7 efficacy weight that would price the 80% neutropenia / 28% febrile-neutropenia trade is an intake default, and the advocate's point stands that this trade has never been put to her. The regimen is the plan her sarcoma oncologist already made, which is the closest thing to a stated goal in the record.
guideline_status: Adoption lag, not opposition: BSG 2025 keeps single-agent doxorubicin at grade I,A and records the combination as 'not yet supported by NICE'; ESMO's operative STS guideline is the 2021 edition and predates the trial; NCCN carriage is confirmed only through secondary sources behind a login wall, so no NCCN category is quoted. Off-label at this line: the trabectedin label requires prior anthracycline.
rationale_summary: All five personas put this first, and for once the aggressive pick, the safe pick and the guideline-adjacent pick are the same regimen: the adjusted PFS HR of 0.41 on a BICR-read pre-specified primary and the 0.65 OS hazard at 55 months are the biggest replicated effect in this dossier, RoB2 Low, in her exact first-line population. The critic and the concensusite converged on the guideline distinction that matters: BSG 2025 holding single-agent doxorubicin at I,A while noting no NICE support is adoption lag plus a reimbursement decision, not a finding against the trial, and the consequence is payer-side rather than clinical, so the authorization is filed as off-label from day one citing both trial publications. The conservative's pre-registered veto was withdrawn with a re-arm clause the synthesis keeps live: if a cycle 1 date is ever placed ahead of the echocardiogram, the veto returns. The maintenance phase is the weakest-evidenced part of the regimen she will spend the longest on: nothing randomises trabectedin continuation against stopping, NCT02997358 has no posted results, the 2024 survival report carries no per-term adverse-event rates, and no preclinical support for the maintenance design exists. Uterine primaries were a stratified subgroup of 67/150 with no separately powered effect estimate, and no replication exists yet; SaLuDo is the nearest confirmatory read and has not reported. Nobody has asked her whether she accepts this toxicity for these gains, because no preference in this case was ever stated.
open_questions: How much of the 12.2-month PFS the maintenance phase contributes; continuation was never randomised against stopping
No uterine-specific effect estimate with its own confidence interval exists (67/150 stratified subgroup)
Whether her ECOG is actually 0-1 and her LVEF adequate; both were trial eligibility criteria and neither is documented
Whether she accepts the 80% / 28% neutropenia trade; the question has not been asked
likelihood_of_effect: High: adjusted HR 0.41 for PFS (BICR primary) and 0.65 for OS in randomized first-line LMS (pmid:35835135, pmid:39231341); maintenance contribution unmeasured.
toxicity_burden: High (G3-4 neutropenia 80%, thrombocytopenia 47%, febrile neutropenia 28%; maintenance-phase transaminitis and rare rhabdomyolysis carried from the single-agent trabectedin dossier)

counter_productive_moa.description: Preclinical pairing was additive at best; untested maintenance continuation could accrue toxicity without measured contribution.

overall: The planned regimen and the best-evidenced option coincide; gated on cardiac clearance and an off-label authorization, with the maintenance phase the least-evidenced part.

scenario_label: If tumor HRR/HRD testing returns deficient (BRCA2-class lesion or functional HRD)
intervention_label: Olaparib + temozolomide, queued for first progression (NCI protocol 10250 regimen), HRR/HRD-conditional
expected_benefit: ORR 27% (best ORR within 6 months 23%) and median PFS 6.9 months (95% CI 5.4-NE) in 22 pretreated advanced uLMS patients, meeting the trial's pre-specified activity bar; exploratory RAD51-foci split of 11.2 vs 5.4 months median PFS (p=0.05, 9/18 evaluable) in HR-deficient vs proficient tumors.
key_risks: G3-4 neutropenia is published two ways: 75% in the abstract and 13/22 (59%) in full-text Table 2; both numbers belong in the consent conversation, and a pre-prescription CBC threshold is required
Thrombocytopenia 32% and anemia 32%; this stacks on marrow that has just absorbed LMS-04 induction (80% G3-4 neutropenia), so documented count recovery precedes any prescription
Dose reductions were frequent, though only 3/22 discontinued for toxicity and no treatment-related deaths were reported
If HRR/HRD testing returns proficient, expected benefit drops toward the 5.4-month arm and the clinical and payer case both weaken
preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist. Oral administration would matter if she turns out to care about infusion-chair time, and nobody knows because nobody asked; prefers_trials true is an intake default and both dedicated trials are closed to accrual anyway, so the interim route is an off-label authorization she has not been asked whether she wants to fight for.
guideline_status: Not guideline-listed; trial-preferred territory. ESMO Precision Medicine Working Group 2024 gives the gating NGS guideline standing. Both dedicated uLMS trials (NCT03880019, NCT05432791) are active-not-recruiting, so access is off-label prescribing on single-arm data until the randomized successor reads out.
rationale_summary: Every persona carried this branch (ranks 2 through 5), making it the consensus second-line bet, and the synthesis queues it for first progression with the HRR panel sent now so the answer is in the chart the day LMS-04 stops working. The critic's ruling on the toxicity discrepancy is adopted whole: the rank was already set by an n=22 single-arm design with no comparator, so the 75%-abstract versus 59%-full-text neutropenia gap does not move the rank, but it changes the consent sentence and the CBC threshold, and both published numbers are quoted. The stratifier that produced the 11.2 vs 5.4 month split is a RAD51-foci functional assay with no CLIA provider anywhere, so the measurable substitute is HRR sequencing, where confirmed HRD ran 5 of 58 uLMS and every confirmed case was a homozygous BRCA2 deletion; presenting the orderable panel as the same test that generated the 11.2-month figure would be false. Both dedicated trials are active-not-recruiting, so the interim route is off-label, and the randomized successor's eligibility (two or more prior lines including an anthracycline, no prior temozolomide or dacarbazine) constrains what can be given in between. If the panel returns proficient, this branch loses most of its case rather than all of it, and that asymmetry is stated on the page rather than hidden in the scenario tag.
open_questions: Her HRR/HRD status; nothing has been sequenced and the branch cannot be priced until it is
Whether a PARP-trial site would run the RAD51 functional assay at screening, since no CLIA catalogue version exists
Marrow reserve after LMS-04 induction and maintenance; the stacking risk is real and unmeasured
Whether NCT05432791 reopens or reports before she needs the decision
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate if HRD confirms: ORR 27%, mPFS 6.9 months on n=22 single-arm (pmid:37467452); exploratory RAD51 split 11.2 vs 5.4 months, assay not orderable.
toxicity_burden: High (G3-4 neutropenia 75% per abstract vs 59% per full-text table, thrombocytopenia 32%, anemia 32%; no treatment-related deaths)

counter_productive_moa.description: In HR-proficient tumors the synergy premise collapses toward temozolomide alone; marrow stacking after induction is the practical brake.

overall: The strongest non-cytotoxic signal in uLMS, opened or mostly closed by an HRR panel nobody has sent; n=22 and an unorderable stratifier bound the confidence.

intervention_label: B7-H3 ADC approach (MGC026, NCT06242470, named sarcoma cohort; approach-level rank consolidating GSK5764227/HS-20093), stain-gated referral at second line or later
expected_benefit: None quotable in LMS: no B7-H3 agent has response data in this histology. The case is target probability (97% of 153 soft-tissue sarcomas stained B7-H3-positive, 69% at high level) plus duocarmycin bystander activity in heterogeneous-expression preclinical models; a positive stain buys a phase 1 referral, not a response estimate.
key_risks: The predecessor vobramitamab duocarmazine was halted after safety findings in prostate cancer; payload liability is the live question for the class
Phase 1 dose escalation with no LMS response data at all; she could be treated at a subtherapeutic dose
Positivity is not dependency: CAR-T antigen-density work shows activity falling away below an expression threshold, so the 69% high-level stratum is the operative number, not the 97%
No standardised clinical scoring for B7-H3 IHC; a local stain may need repeating on the sponsor's assay at screening
preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist; prefers_trials true is an intake default. The advocate's hold applies: the stain runs during induction at no cost, but no referral gets booked until her trial appetite and travel tolerance from 8,500 ft are asked directly.
guideline_status: No guideline mentions B7-H3-directed therapy in sarcoma; guideline silence licenses trial screening (BSG 2025 builds specialist care around trial recruitment) but supplies no compendium listing and no payer path outside the trial.
rationale_summary: The risktaker's best experimental door: B7-H3 is the surface target most likely to actually be there in this histology, the stain costs two slides off a block already being cut, and MGC026 is recruiting US sites with sarcoma on the named list and no expression gate. The critic's counter is carried at full weight: 97% positivity is prevalence, not dependency, the number that tracked response in the antigen-density work was expression above a threshold, and no LMS model exists for any B7-H3 agent in this dossier. The conservative's missing-baseline objection extends here from its FAP dissent: a phase 1 referral against marrow that has just absorbed LMS-04, with no CBC on file, is premature until counts are documented. The class also carries a corpse, since MacroGenics' previous B7-H3 ADC was terminated on safety findings, and that liability transfers to the successor until its own data say otherwise. The synthesis lands where the risktaker did after concessions: run the stain during induction, book nothing until the trial and travel questions are asked, and treat a strong positive as the most reachable experimental door at second or third line.
open_questions: Her B7-H3 expression level; unmeasured, and the high-expression stratum is what matters
Whether MGC026 escapes the payload liability that terminated vobramitamab
Her trial appetite and travel tolerance from 8,500 ft; never asked
Marrow recovery after induction, on a CBC that has never been drawn
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown in LMS: no clinical efficacy for any B7-H3 agent; 97% sarcoma positivity with 69% high (pmid:39478506) makes the gating stain worth one slide.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (no published MGC026 grade profile; predecessor duocarmycin ADC halted on safety findings; ADC-class cytopenias and infusion reactions expected)

counter_productive_moa.description: Positivity is not dependency; activity fell away below an antigen-density threshold, so low expressors likely gain little.

overall: The most reachable experimental door if the stain is strongly positive, on a target class whose predecessor died on safety and which has no LMS response data.

intervention_label: FAP-targeted radioligand approach ([225Ac]RTX-2358, NCT07156565, FAPi-PET-gated; approach-level rank consolidating [177Lu]Lu-FAP-2286 / LuMIERE), screen at first progression
expected_benefit: None quotable in humans for this agent. The case is mechanism fit: sarcoma sits near the top of the FAP expression range with tumour-cell FAP at intensity >=2 in 50.7% of sarcomas (the malignant cell is itself fibroblastic), radioligand crossfire does not depend on the antigen homogeneity that undermines ADC and cell-therapy cutoffs, and 177Lu-FAP-2286 produced regressions in sarcoma PDX models. A FAPi PET scan settles whether the target exists at no tissue cost.
key_risks: FAP sits on bone marrow stromal cells and FAP-directed CAR-T caused cachexia and lethal marrow toxicity in mice; whether that transfers to a renally cleared peptide is a dosimetry question NCT07156565 has not answered
Phase 1 dose escalation with no human sarcoma efficacy for this specific agent
Sequencing an alpha emitter after an induction that ran 80% G3-4 neutropenia requires a documented marrow baseline and recovery; no CBC exists yet
ECOG 0-1 required against an ECOG that was assumed at intake, never documented
preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist; the same hold applies as for every trial door, since prefers_trials true was never her statement and the screening logistics involve travel from 8,500 ft.
guideline_status: No guideline carriage; trial-only. The FAPi PET gate itself is investigational imaging.
rationale_summary: The one phase-1 pick where the round-2 exchange sharpened rather than sank the case. The conservative dissented on the marrow-stroma signal: FAP-directed effectors recognised human marrow stromal cells and killed mice, and pointing an alpha emitter at that target in a patient whose CBC has never been drawn, straight after a heavily myelotoxic induction, is a real objection. The risktaker's counters are also real: tumour-cell FAP is present at meaningful intensity in half of sarcomas because the malignant cell is fibroblastic, a renally cleared peptide is a different exposure question from a persisting engineered T cell, and the FAPi PET gate can return negative at no cost to her. The adjudication keeps the option ranked as a screen-first branch: the PET scan and the marrow baseline are both cheap and the baseline is already ordered at rank 1, while any treatment decision waits on human marrow-stroma dosimetry from the trial itself and a documented count recovery. It sits above REC-617 because its gate runs forward (a positive scan means the target is there) where the RB1 stain most likely routes her into an arm with no LMS data, and below B7-H3 because the marrow-stroma toxicity signal is an on-target concern the ADC class does not carry.
open_questions: FAPi PET uptake in her tumours; unmeasured, and the scan is the whole eligibility question
Human marrow-stroma dosimetry for [225Ac]RTX-2358; the mouse signal has no human read yet
Marrow reserve after induction, on a CBC that has never been drawn
Whether the beta-emitter LuMIERE route (177Lu-FAP-2286) offers a gentler first pass if uptake is confirmed
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: no human sarcoma efficacy for this agent; tumour-cell FAP >=2 intensity in 50.7% of sarcomas (pmid:37333052) and PDX regressions support the screen.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (no human grade profile; on-target marrow-stroma concern from FAP CAR-T mouse work; radioligand-class cytopenias expected)

counter_productive_moa.description: FAP sits on marrow stroma; the crossfire that beats tumour heterogeneity reaches it too, so dosimetry rather than IHC decides.

overall: A forward-running gate at zero tissue cost: a FAPi PET either finds the target or closes the branch, with marrow-stroma dosimetry the open safety question.

intervention_label: REC-617 (selective CDK7 inhibitor) after RB1-null IHC, second line (NCT07633756, single site)
expected_benefit: None quotable: no CDK7 data of any kind exist in leiomyosarcoma at any phase. The mechanistic case (RB1-null replication stress) is borrowed from YKL-5-124 in RB1/TP53-null small-cell lung cancer, a different compound in a different lineage. A positive would be first-in-class access for her genotype after one prior line.
key_risks: Phase 1b dose escalation with a safety primary endpoint; she could be treated at a subtherapeutic dose
Requires a biopsy-amenable lesion and RECIST-measurable disease, both uncertain against her infiltrative pulmonary pattern
Single site (Houston); travel burden from an 8,500 ft residence unquantified and her travel tolerance never asked
The gating stain runs backwards: RB1 loss is near-universal in this histology, so a null result most likely routes her into the arm with zero LMS data
preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist; this pick leans hardest on the prefers_trials intake default, which is exactly the value the advocate flagged as never hers. The stain runs during induction at no cost; the referral waits on her answers.
guideline_status: No guideline mentions CDK7 inhibition in sarcoma. Guideline silence licenses trial screening but supplies no compendium listing and no payer path when the stain, the biopsy requirement, or the Houston logistics fail; the on-label second-line anchor (pazopanib) lives on the Standard-of-care table.
rationale_summary: Ranked, but at the bottom of the experimental doors, on the structural argument the risktaker itself conceded: because RB1 loss is near-universal in LMS, the stain that gates this trial most likely routes her toward the arm holding no leiomyosarcoma data at all, so the gate runs backwards, and the pick belongs below B7-H3. The critic's evidence objection stands unreduced: the mechanism is borrowed from a different compound in a different lineage, and no CDK7 data exist in LMS at any phase. The concensusite's dissent lands on the slate rather than the agent: a run of phase 1 doors with no on-label anchor around them leaves nothing a payer recognizes when the gates fail, which is why the approved second-line backbone sits on the Standard-of-care table where it belongs. The conservative's missing-baseline problem applies here as everywhere in the investigational block. What survives is cheap and real: the RB1 stain costs one slide on a block already being cut, and a null result plus an asked-and-answered travel question makes this a live second-line door rather than a paper one.
open_questions: Her RB1 status; unmeasured, and near-universal loss in this histology cuts both ways
Whether the trial's LMS arm accrues any response signal before she would need it
Whether her pulmonary disease pattern yields a biopsy-amenable, RECIST-measurable target
Her trial appetite and travel tolerance from 8,500 ft; never asked
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: zero CDK7 data in LMS; mechanism borrowed from RB1-null SCLC with a different compound (pmid:31883968). Phase 1b, safety primary.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (no published REC-617 grade profile; CDK7-class cytopenias and GI toxicity expected; dose escalation design)

counter_productive_moa.description: The gating stain routes a near-universally RB1-null histology into the arm with no LMS data; mechanism is cross-lineage borrowed.

overall: A one-slide stain opens a first-in-class door, but the gate runs backwards in this histology and the arm it opens holds no LMS data.

intervention_label: Abemaciclib + gemcitabine (NCT06498648, first-line LMS cohort) — considered and declined
expected_benefit: None quotable: phase 1/2 with no LMS efficacy readout. It was the only recruiting first-line trial in the dossier taking systemic-treatment-naive LMS, which is why the advocate listed it; only prior gemcitabine is barred, so the door technically stays open after LMS-04.
key_risks: The concurrent schedule contradicts its own mechanism: CDK4/6 inhibition protected RB-proficient cells from concurrent genotoxic therapy, with viable populations recurring afterwards
The priming schedule that did work in Rb-positive LMS xenografts was sequential, and it is not the schedule this trial runs
Both drugs are myelosuppressive with no characterized combination safety data in LMS, against an undrawn CBC and an altitude-confounded haemoglobin
A chemo-naive phase 1/2 slot would spend the asset that buys the randomized 33-month arm
preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist. The pick existed to force a question that still stands: whether she wants trials at all, and how far she will travel from 8,500 ft, must be asked before prefers_trials true hardens into her chart.
guideline_status: Investigational; no guideline carriage. First-line trial enrollment would displace the guideline-adjacent planned regimen.
rationale_summary: Recorded as considered and declined, with the withdrawal on the record rather than the pick silently dropped. The advocate ranked it fourth solely because it was the one recruiting first-line study taking treatment-naive LMS and because nobody has asked her whether she wants a trial; after the critic and the risktaker independently raised the concurrent-schedule contradiction, the advocate conceded and withdrew it as the vehicle. The mechanism problem is schedule-specific and therefore decisive for this protocol: CDK4/6 inhibition protects RB-proficient cells from concurrent genotoxic therapy, while the priming that worked in Rb-positive LMS xenografts was sequential, and NCT06498648 runs the drugs concurrently. The conservative added the marrow math: two myelosuppressives with no combination safety data in LMS, met with no baseline CBC and an altitude-raised haemoglobin that hides anaemia until it is deep. The question the pick existed to force is preserved at rank 1 and in the caveats: her trial appetite and travel tolerance were never asked, and that conversation happens regardless of this trial's fate.
open_questions: Her trial appetite and travel tolerance from 8,500 ft; the question this pick existed to force, still unasked
Whether a sequential-priming CDK4/6 protocol ever opens in LMS; that schedule has the preclinical support this one lacks
likelihood_of_effect: Not assessable: no LMS efficacy data, and the concurrent schedule contradicts the sequential-priming evidence (pmid:22751436, pmid:28619757) that motivated the pairing.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (no combination safety data in LMS; overlapping myelosuppression from both agents expected)

counter_productive_moa.description: Concurrent CDK4/6 inhibition shields RB-proficient cells from gemcitabine, the opposite of the sequential priming that worked in LMS xenografts.

overall: Declined by its own sponsor persona: the schedule argues against its own mechanism, and the chemo-naive slot it would spend is the asset that buys the 33-month arm.

intervention_label: GSK5764227 / HS-20093 (B7-H3 ADC; EMBOLD NCT06551142, ARTEMIS-002 NCT05830123)
expected_benefit: None quotable for this patient; surfaced for completeness, not ranked as a live option.
preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist; no preference filter applies.
rationale_summary: One product of the B7-H3 ADC approach ranked once at rank 4. EMBOLD recruits advanced solid tumours after standard therapy and ARTEMIS-002 runs a sarcoma cohort, but the ARTEMIS sites are in China and neither trial names LMS the way the MGC026 protocol does. If the rank-4 stain is strongly positive and MGC026 screening fails, this is the same door under a different sponsor.
likelihood_of_effect: See rank 4: the approach is ranked once; no LMS response data for any B7-H3 agent.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (topoisomerase-payload ADC class profile; no LMS-specific data)

counter_productive_moa.description: Same antigen-density dependency as the ranked B7-H3 approach.

overall: The backup sponsor for the rank-4 approach, reachable mainly outside the US.

intervention_label: [177Lu]Lu-FAP-2286 (beta-emitting FAP radioligand; LuMIERE NCT04939610)
expected_benefit: None quotable for this patient; surfaced for completeness, not ranked as a live option.
preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist; no preference filter applies.
rationale_summary: One product of the FAP radioligand approach ranked once at rank 5. The preclinical regressions in sarcoma PDX models that anchor the class belong to this compound, and LuMIERE is recruiting with FAP-2286 uptake as its own PET gate. A beta emitter is the gentler physics if marrow-stroma exposure turns out to matter; the same FAPi PET screen prices both doors at once.
likelihood_of_effect: See rank 5: the approach is ranked once; sarcoma PDX regressions (pmid:35608703) belong to this compound.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (no human sarcoma grade profile; radioligand-class cytopenias expected)

counter_productive_moa.description: Same marrow-stroma FAP exposure question as the ranked alpha emitter, at lower per-decay energy.

overall: The beta-emitter form of the rank-5 approach, and possibly the gentler first pass if uptake confirms.

intervention_label: Vobramitamab duocarmazine (B7-H3 duocarmycin ADC; NCT05551117, terminated)
expected_benefit: None quotable for this patient; surfaced for completeness, not ranked as a live option.
preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist; no preference filter applies.
rationale_summary: The predecessor whose preclinical bystander data support the rank-4 class and whose clinical termination haunts it. MacroGenics halted the programme after safety findings in prostate cancer. It is surfaced because the payload-liability question it left open is the live risk carried on the rank-4 row, not because any route to it exists.
likelihood_of_effect: Not obtainable: programme terminated on safety findings; its bystander data (pmid:37775116) are why the class stays interesting.
toxicity_burden: High (programme halted after safety findings in the TAMARACK context)

counter_productive_moa.description: The payload liability that ended this programme may be a class property; the successor has not yet shown otherwise.

overall: The corpse in the B7-H3 class: its preclinical data motivate rank 4 and its termination is rank 4's biggest caveat.

intervention_label: Ivonescimab (PD-1 x VEGF bispecific; NCT07516925, phase 2 LMS, 1-3 prior lines)
expected_benefit: None quotable for this patient; surfaced for completeness, not ranked as a live option.
preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist; no preference filter applies.
rationale_summary: Recruiting phase 2 in unresectable or metastatic LMS with an ORR primary and no LMS efficacy published yet. The protocol admits patients who declined first-line standard of care, but no persona would spend her chemotherapy-naive slot here against a randomized 33 vs 24 month OS benefit. A legitimate second-line screening conversation once LMS-04 progresses and the trial has any readout.
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: no LMS efficacy data for the construct; recruiting with ORR primary.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (PD-1 and VEGF class toxicities: immune-related AEs, hypertension, proteinuria)

counter_productive_moa.description: No mechanism objection raised; checkpoint activity in unselected LMS has historically been modest.

overall: A recruiting LMS-named phase 2 for the post-LMS-04 conversation, with nothing published to weigh yet.

intervention_label: All-trans retinoic acid + cemiplimab (NCT06528769, phase 2 LMS after standard chemotherapy)
expected_benefit: None quotable for this patient; surfaced for completeness, not ranked as a live option.
preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist; no preference filter applies.
rationale_summary: Recruiting phase 2 in advanced LMS after standard-of-care chemotherapy, resting on ATRA's myeloid-derived-suppressor-cell differentiation mechanism from mouse work two decades old. No LMS efficacy data exist for the combination. Surfaced as a second-line trial door that costs nothing today and should be re-checked at progression.
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: no clinical efficacy for the combination in LMS; mechanism rests on preclinical MDSC work (pmid:12907617).
toxicity_burden: Moderate (checkpoint-class immune-related AEs plus ATRA headache, dryness, hypertriglyceridemia)

counter_productive_moa.description: No mechanism objection raised; the MDSC-differentiation premise is untested in sarcoma patients.

overall: A mechanism-first checkpoint combination recruiting in her disease, with the evidence still entirely preclinical.

intervention_label: Zanzalintinib (XL092 multi-kinase TKI; NCT06571734, phase 2 LMS cohort, >=2 prior lines)
expected_benefit: None quotable for this patient; surfaced for completeness, not ranked as a live option.
preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist; no preference filter applies.
rationale_summary: Recruiting phase 2 with an LMS cohort at third line or later, no LMS data published. The TKI class already has an approved, guideline-carried member (pazopanib) that lives on the Standard-of-care table and is the payer-recognized comparator any zanzalintinib slot would have to beat. Re-check at the third-line decision point.
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown in LMS: no published data; the approved class comparator (pazopanib) sets the bar on the Standard-of-care table.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (VEGFR-TKI class: hypertension, diarrhea, fatigue, hand-foot syndrome)

counter_productive_moa.description: No mechanism objection; class wound-healing impairment would matter if metastasectomy ever became real.

overall: A third-line TKI trial door whose whole case is beating an approved drug that already exists for the same slot.

intervention_label: IMA203 / IMA203CD8 (PRAME TCR-T, HLA-A*02:01-restricted; NCT03686124)
expected_benefit: None quotable for this patient; surfaced for completeness, not ranked as a live option.
preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist; no preference filter applies.
rationale_summary: Double-gated and unpriceable today: neither her HLA type nor tumour PRAME expression has been measured, and reported PRAME expression in LMS runs below the synovial sarcoma levels the class was built on. The rank-1 workup includes HLA typing with reflex PRAME IHC if a restricting allele returns, which prices this door for the cost of a blood draw and two slides.
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: both gates (HLA-A*02:01 and PRAME expression) unmeasured; LMS PRAME prior runs low.
toxicity_burden: High (TCR-T class: cytokine release syndrome, lymphodepletion cytopenias)

counter_productive_moa.description: Antigen-loss escape and low LMS PRAME density are the class risks; no persona assessed it.

overall: A cell-therapy door that costs a blood draw and two slides to price, with a low prior in this histology.

intervention_label: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd; DESTINY-PanTumor02 basket, NCT04482309)
expected_benefit: None quotable for this patient; surfaced for completeness, not ranked as a live option.
preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist; no preference filter applies.
rationale_summary: Gated on a HER2 stain nobody has run, in a histology DESTINY-PanTumor02 did not include. The tumor-agnostic approval sits at IHC 3+, so a 3+ result would route this to the Standard-of-care table as an on-label option; anything lower is cross-tumor extrapolation with no sarcoma cohort behind it. The stain can join the bundled IHC pass if the treating team wants the question closed.
likelihood_of_effect: Low prior: HER2 unmeasured, no sarcoma cohort in DESTINY-PanTumor02 (pmid:37870536); IHC 3+ would change the table it belongs on.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis, a named risk against bilateral infiltrative lung disease; cytopenias, nausea)

counter_productive_moa.description: Drug-related pneumonitis would be unreadable against her infiltrative lung disease and altitude-shifted oximetry.

overall: An unmeasured gate with a low prior, and a pneumonitis liability her lungs are poorly placed to absorb.

intervention_label: Trabectedin + olaparib (preclinical combination; PARP1-expression-dependent synergy)
expected_benefit: None quotable for this patient; surfaced for completeness, not ranked as a live option.
preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist; no preference filter applies.
rationale_summary: A preclinical pairing whose synergy tracked PARP1 expression in sarcoma models, with no clinical vehicle in this dossier and PARP1 expression never measured in her. Surfaced because the maintenance phase of the rank-2 regimen and the rank-3 PARP branch make the mechanistic overlap worth knowing about, not because anyone can prescribe it.
likelihood_of_effect: Not assessable: preclinical only (pmid:28454547); the proposed predictor, PARP1 expression, has never been measured in her.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (would stack trabectedin hepatotoxicity on PARP-inhibitor cytopenias; no clinical characterization)

counter_productive_moa.description: No mechanism objection; the combination is untested rather than contradicted.

overall: A preclinical synergy note connecting the rank-2 and rank-3 mechanisms, with no trial to put it in.

intervention_label: ATR inhibition for ATRX-loss / ALT-positive tumors (mechanism hypothesis)
expected_benefit: None quotable for this patient; surfaced for completeness, not ranked as a live option.
preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist; no preference filter applies.
rationale_summary: The original claim that ALT-positive cells are hypersensitive to ATR inhibition failed replication twice, and ATRX loss or ALT prevalence in uLMS is prevalence, not dependency. Her ATRX status is unmeasured; the NGS panel and the paired ATRX IHC in the workup will report it for prognosis. The critic's round-1 verdict stands: not a branch this board would fund.
likelihood_of_effect: Low: the founding sensitivity claim (pmid:25593184) failed replication twice (pmid:27602331, pmid:33344901).
toxicity_burden: Low (no clinical vehicle in this dossier to attach a grade profile to)

counter_productive_moa.description: The founding synthetic-lethality claim did not replicate, so the mechanism may simply not be there.

overall: A twice-failed replication wearing a plausible mechanism; the workup reports ATRX for prognosis, not for this.

intervention_label: Lurbinectedin + doxorubicin (SaLuDo phase 3, NCT06088290, first-line LMS)
expected_benefit: None quotable for this patient; surfaced for completeness, not ranked as a live option.
preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist; no preference filter applies.
rationale_summary: Active-not-recruiting with no posted results, so there is no slot to enrol into and no number to weigh. It is surfaced because it is the nearest confirmatory read on the rank-2 design question (a trabectedin-class minor-groove binder added to doxorubicin, first line) and its readout is worth watching from maintenance.
likelihood_of_effect: Not enrollable: closed to accrual, no results posted; informational as the nearest LMS-04 replication read.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (expected to mirror anthracycline-plus-minor-groove-binder myelosuppression; no published rates)

counter_productive_moa.description: No mechanism objection; the open question is replication, not antagonism.

overall: The trial whose readout will either replicate the rank-2 effect in class or complicate it; watch, cannot join.

preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist; no preference filter applies.
rationale_summary: The named sarcoma protocol restricts to synovial sarcoma and myxoid round cell liposarcoma and is not yet recruiting, so LMS has no route in. The PRAME thread itself stays alive through the rank-1 HLA typing and reflex PRAME IHC, which is all this row costs to keep warm.
likelihood_of_effect: Not enrollable: the sarcoma protocol excludes LMS; PRAME and HLA both unmeasured besides.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (ImmTAC-class cytokine release and skin toxicity expected)

intervention_label: Afamitresgene autoleucel (MAGE-A4 TCR-T, approved in synovial sarcoma / MRCLS; SPEARHEAD-1)
expected_benefit: None quotable for this patient; surfaced for completeness, not ranked as a live option.
preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist; no preference filter applies.
rationale_summary: Approved, but for synovial sarcoma and MRCLS rather than any population that includes her, so it cannot route to the Standard-of-care table and has no LMS label to prescribe against. MAGE-A4 expression in LMS runs below the synovial levels the product was built on, and both her HLA type and antigen status are unmeasured. The realistic destination, if the reflex stains ever turn positive, is a cross-histology MAGE-A4 trial rather than this product.
likelihood_of_effect: Not applicable to LMS: licensed indication excludes her histology; both gates unmeasured and the antigen prior is low.
toxicity_burden: High (TCR-T class: cytokine release syndrome in most patients in SPEARHEAD-1, cytopenias)

counter_productive_moa.description: Low MAGE-A4 antigen density in LMS is the class problem; no persona assessed it.

overall: An approved cell therapy pointed at a different sarcoma; for her it is two stains and a typing result away from even being a question.

toxicity_burden: Moderate (VEGFR-TKI class: hypertension, hand-foot syndrome, fatigue)

intervention_label: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin maintenance (MELODY NCT06981637, Taiwan)

rationale_summary: The one randomized trial asking the maintenance question that the rank-2 regimen leaves open (continue versus surveillance after first-line anthracycline disease control), recruiting in Taiwan only. She cannot join it; its readout bears directly on the least-evidenced phase of her planned regimen and is worth watching.
likelihood_of_effect: Not enrollable (geography): Taiwan-only; informational for the maintenance question the rank-2 regimen cannot answer.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (PLD class: hand-foot syndrome, mucositis, cumulative cardiac exposure)

counter_productive_moa.description: No mechanism objection; the relevance is the maintenance design question, not the drug.

intervention_label: Pulmonary suffusion + metastasectomy (NCT03965234, phase 1/2 feasibility)
expected_benefit: None quotable for this patient; surfaced for completeness, not ranked as a live option.
preference_alignment: No stated preferences exist; no preference filter applies.
rationale_summary: A feasibility-and-safety study attached to a consolidation branch she is not currently a candidate for: the metastasectomy literature screened out bilateral infiltrative disease, which is her pattern, and the morcellation record retrieved at rank 1 gates the whole branch besides. If induction converts her anatomy, the local-therapy question gets re-asked on the Standard-of-care table, and this trial can be re-checked then.
likelihood_of_effect: Not currently a candidate: bilateral infiltrative disease is what the surgical series screened out; feasibility endpoint only.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (thoracic surgical morbidity; no efficacy-grade data)

counter_productive_moa.description: No mechanism objection; anatomy and staging are the gates.

overall: A surgical-adjunct trial for an anatomy she does not currently have, behind a staging question the workup settles.
